cut_surface_roughness — DRIVE cutting op

• Data kinds: rgb × scalar × scalar × signal → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.cut_surface_roughness(image, px_per_mm: 'float', board_row: 'float', z_band, n_sampling: 'int' = 5) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import cutting; cutting.cut_surface_roughness(image, px_per_mm: 'float', board_row: 'float', z_band, n_sampling: 'int' = 5) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("cut_surface_roughness"))

Usage

Treats the silhouette of the end face after cutting (subpixel per row) as a profile, fits a least-squares line and outputs ISO 4287 parameters (µm).

The parameters call roughness.profile_params (Ra / Rq / Rz / Rt …) as is. The profile is averaged over a row height of 1 px, so sinusoidal relief is attenuated by the box-shaped closed form sinc(πΔ/λ) (Δ = 1 px). Even a flat surface leaves a measurement floor (Rq due to noise and texture), so subtract the floor in quadrature when comparing. Rz is pulled by noise peaks (handling the floor is meaningful only for Rq). Return value: profile_um (per-row deviation), z_mm, params, dz_um (sampling interval), n_rows.
